concepts.title: Congiuntivo presente after opinion, emotion, wish and doubt
concepts.rule: Verbs of opinion, emotion, wish, doubt and impersonal judgements (penso che, sono contento che, voglio che, dubito che, è possibile che) take the subjunctive. Verbs of certainty (so che, è chiaro che, sono sicuro che) take the indicative.
assessment: Chooses the subjunctive after opinion, emotion, wish, fear and doubt verbs
Chooses the indicative after verbs and expressions of certainty
Forms the present subjunctive of regular and common irregular verbs correctly
Produces subjunctive clauses when translating from English, where English shows no difference

lesson.intro: English rarely marks the subjunctive ("I think she **is** right"), so English speakers tend to slip into the indicative. In Italian the main verb decides: if it expresses a **personal view, feeling, wish or uncertainty**, the verb after *che* goes into the **congiuntivo**. If it presents something as **fact or certainty**, use the indicative. In careful and formal Italian, getting this right is one of the clearest markers of a C1 speaker.

rules.title: Triggers: subjunctive after che
rules.text: Opinion: *penso, credo, mi sembra, mi pare, ritengo, immagino che*. Emotion: *sono contento, mi dispiace, ho paura, temo, è strano che*. Wish or will: *voglio, spero, preferisco, desidero che*. Doubt: *dubito, non sono sicuro, non è detto che*. Impersonal judgement: *è possibile, è importante, bisogna, è meglio, è normale che*.

examples.it: È importante che tutti **sappiano** la verità.
examples.en: It's important that everyone knows the truth.

rules.title: Certainty takes the indicative
rules.text: *So che, sono sicuro che, è chiaro / evidente / vero che, dimostra che, vedo che* present a fact, so they take the **indicative**. Overusing the subjunctive here is an error too, often made by advanced learners.

examples.it: È evidente che la situazione **è** cambiata.
examples.en: It's obvious the situation has changed.

rules.title: Forms: congiuntivo presente
rules.text: -are verbs: *-i, -i, -i, -iamo, -iate, -ino* (parli). -ere/-ire verbs: *-a, -a, -a, -iamo, -iate, -ano* (prenda, dorma, capisca). The three singular forms are identical, so add the subject pronoun when it isn't clear (*che io / tu / lei vada*). The **noi** form is the same as the indicative (*perdiamo*).

rules.title: Same subject: use di + infinitive
rules.text: When the subject of both verbs is the same, Italian uses *di* + infinitive, not *che* + subjunctive: *Penso **di avere** ragione* (not ~~penso che io abbia~~). Exceptions: *volere, preferire, desiderare* take a bare infinitive (*Voglio partire*).

examples.en: I hope to see you soon.

mistakes.why: Opinion verb: needs the subjunctive. *Penso che è* is common in fast speech but marked as sub-standard.
*Sapere* states a fact, so it takes the indicative.
*Stare* and *dare* have irregular stems: *stia, dia*, never *stii, dii*.
Same subject in both clauses: use *di* + infinitive.

tips: Quick test: can you add 'I'm certain that…' without changing the meaning? If so, use the indicative.
In informal speech you'll hear *penso che è*. Recognise it, but don't write it.

exercises.instruction: Complete with the correct form of the verb in brackets.
exercises.prompt: Penso che Marco ___ (avere) ragione.

traps.why: *Penso che* expresses an opinion, so it needs the subjunctive: *abbia*.

exercises.instruction: Complete with the correct form of the verb in brackets.
exercises.prompt: Mi sembra che tu ___ (essere) un po' stanco oggi.

traps.why: *Mi sembra che* is an impression or opinion, so it takes the subjunctive: *(tu) sia*.

exercises.en: It seems to me you're a bit tired today.

exercises.instruction: Complete with the correct form of the verb in brackets.
exercises.prompt: Sono contenta che voi ___ (venire) alla festa.

traps.why: Emotion (*sono contenta che*) needs the subjunctive: *veniate*.
The voi form keeps the regular stem: *veniate* (compare *vengano* for loro).

exercises.explanation: Emotion + che → congiuntivo. *Venire*: venga, venga, venga, veniamo, **veniate**, vengano.
exercises.en: I'm glad you (all) are coming to the party.

exercises.instruction: Complete with the correct form of the verb in brackets.
exercises.prompt: Dubito che loro ___ (sapere) la verità.

traps.why: Doubt (*dubito che*) needs the subjunctive.
*Sapere* has an irregular subjunctive stem with a double p: *sappia, sappiano*.

exercises.en: I doubt they know the truth.

exercises.instruction: Complete with the correct form of the verb in brackets.
exercises.prompt: Temo che Giulia non ___ (stare) bene.

traps.why: Fear (*temo che*) takes the subjunctive.
*Stare* → *stia*, not *stii* (same pattern as *dare* → *dia*).

exercises.instruction: Complete with the correct form of the verb in brackets.
exercises.prompt: È possibile che il treno ___ (fare) ritardo.

traps.why: *È possibile che* is an impersonal judgement of possibility, so it takes the subjunctive.

exercises.instruction: Complete with the correct form of the verb in brackets.
exercises.prompt: Credo che i ragazzi ___ (dovere) studiare di più.

traps.why: *Credo che* + subjunctive. *Dovere* → *debbano*.
*Devano* is non-standard. The standard form is *debbano*.

exercises.en: I think the boys need to study more.

exercises.instruction: Complete with the correct form of the verb in brackets.
exercises.prompt: Spero che tu ___ (potere) venire sabato.

traps.why: *Sperare che* expresses a wish: subjunctive *possa*.

exercises.en: I hope you can come on Saturday.

exercises.instruction: Complete with the correct form of the verb in brackets.
exercises.prompt: Non sono sicuro che lei ___ (capire) il problema.

traps.why: *Non sono sicuro* expresses uncertainty, so it needs the subjunctive. Note that *sono sicuro che* (certainty) takes the indicative.
-isc- verbs keep -isc- in the singular: *capisca*.

exercises.en: I'm not sure she understands the problem.

exercises.instruction: Complete with the correct form of the verb in brackets.
exercises.prompt: Ho paura che noi ___ (perdere) il treno.

traps.why: That's the voi form. Here the subject is noi: *perdiamo*.
The main verb is present (*ho paura*), so use the present subjunctive, not the imperfect.

exercises.explanation: Trick question: the **noi** form of the present subjunctive is identical to the indicative: *perdiamo*.
exercises.en: I'm afraid we'll miss the train.

exercises.instruction: Complete with the correct form of the verb in brackets.
exercises.prompt: Immagino che voi ___ (essere) stanchi dopo il viaggio.

traps.why: *Immagino che* is a supposition, so it takes the subjunctive: *siate*.

exercises.en: I imagine you're tired after the journey.

exercises.instruction: Indicative or subjunctive? Complete with the correct form.
exercises.prompt: So che Marco ___ (avere) ragione.

traps.why: *Sapere* expresses certainty, not opinion: indicative *ha*.

exercises.instruction: Indicative or subjunctive? Complete with the correct form.
exercises.prompt: È evidente che la situazione ___ (essere) cambiata.

traps.why: *È evidente che* presents a fact: indicative *è (cambiata)*.

exercises.explanation: Impersonal expressions of **certainty** (è evidente / chiaro / vero che) → indicativo.
exercises.en: It's obvious the situation has changed.

exercises.instruction: Choose the correct form.
exercises.prompt: Voglio che tu mi ___ la verità.

traps.why: *Volere che* (will) takes the subjunctive.
*Dicessi* is imperfect subjunctive, used after a past or conditional main verb (*Volevo / Vorrei che tu dicessi*). Here *voglio* is present.
Future indicative isn't possible after *volere che*.

exercises.en: I want you to tell me the truth.

exercises.instruction: Translate into Italian.
exercises.prompt: I think she is right.

traps.why: After *penso / credo che*, *ha* becomes subjunctive *abbia*.
'To be right' is *avere ragione* in Italian, not *essere*.

exercises.instruction: Translate into Italian (informal 'you').
exercises.prompt: I'm glad you're here.
answers: (Sono contento|Sono contenta|Sono felice|Mi fa piacere) che [tu] sia qui
(Sono contento|Sono contenta|Sono felice|Mi fa piacere) che [tu] sia qua

traps.why: Emotion + che → subjunctive: *(tu) sia*.
Use the informal singular, *tu*, and the subjunctive: *sia*.

exercises.instruction: Rewrite the sentence starting with 'Penso che…'.
exercises.prompt: Paolo arriva stasera.

traps.why: After *penso che*, *arriva* → *arrivi* (-are verbs take -i).
*Penso che Paolo arriverà stasera* is also used, because the future can replace the subjunctive for future events. The present subjunctive *arrivi* is the target form here.

exercises.en: I think Paolo is arriving tonight.

exercises.instruction: Translate into Italian.
exercises.prompt: It's strange that nobody is answering.
answers: È strano che non risponda nessuno
È strano che nessuno stia rispondendo

traps.why: *È strano che* (emotional judgement) → subjunctive *risponda*.
The progressive also needs the subjunctive: *stia rispondendo*.

exercises.en: It's strange that nobody is answering.

exercises.instruction: Put the words in order.
exercises.prompt: I hope you (all) enjoy yourselves at the party.
answers: Spero che vi divertiate alla festa
exercises.explanation: The reflexive pronoun *vi* goes before the conjugated verb: *che vi divertiate*.

exercises.instruction: Rewrite using 'di' + infinitive where the subject is the same.
exercises.prompt: Penso che io abbia sbagliato.

traps.why: Same subject (io… io) → *di* + infinitive, no *che*.

exercises.explanation: Same subject → *penso di* + (past) infinitive: *di aver(e) sbagliato*.
